## [0.6.4] - 2026-09-01

### Added

- The published container image (`ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto`) is now multi-arch - `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` under one tag, so self-hosting on arm64 hardware (AWS Graviton, Oracle Cloud's free arm tier, Raspberry Pi-class devices, Apple Silicon via Docker Desktop) pulls a native image instead of needing QEMU emulation or failing outright. Both platforms go through the same Trivy CRITICAL-vulnerability gate before either is pushed.
- Reports has a new "Wallets" tab: wallet adoption and platform-mix breakdowns, adoption by ticket type, cumulative passes issued, time from ticket email to wallet install, and check-in rate compared between attendees with and without a wallet pass. "Export report" now follows whichever tab is open - the Wallets tab exports a CSV with one row per attendee's wallet status (issued/installed/voided, per-platform registration, check-in) or a printable PDF summary, instead of always exporting Event day's admission log regardless of which tab was showing.
- Reports has a new "Custom fields" tab, with one chart per custom field configured on the event's Requirements page: a select or yes/no field gets a donut breakdown of how many attendees hold each value (plus a slice for how many haven't answered yet), and a free-text field gets a single-ring gauge showing how many attendees have filled it in. The chart type follows the field's own type automatically, so a newly added custom field gets a chart here with no extra setup.
- Settings → Security has a new "Passkey / security key sign-in" toggle, exposing the existing instance-wide passkey/security-key feature (previously configurable only via an environment variable) directly in the admin UI. A second new toggle, "Passkey sign-in on the login page", adds a "Sign in with a passkey" option to the sign-in screen: staff with a registered passkey can sign in with it directly, skipping the password entirely, without giving up second-factor strength - a verified passkey satisfies two-factor authentication on its own. The password field is never removed; it stays available either way, and a security key (as opposed to a passkey) still only works at the existing two-factor step, not here.
- Editing a select-type custom field's options is now a structured list instead of a plain "one per line" textarea. Each option shows how many attendees currently have it selected, warns in place before a rename that would affect them, asks for confirmation before removing an option that's in use, and blocks Save behind a summary of anything risky an operator hasn't explicitly acknowledged. Options can also be reordered by drag (mouse, touch, or pen) or, with the drag handle focused, the up/down arrow keys.
- Check-in's camera scanner gained a torch toggle, next to the existing mute/close controls on both the mobile full-screen scanner and the desktop/tablet inline camera. Only appears once the active camera actually reports the capability, since most laptop webcams and every iPhone don't - so it stays out of the way rather than sitting there doing nothing.
- Communication → Send now has a "Stop" button while a bulk send is draining, so an operator who spots a mistake (wrong template, typo, wrong audience) can halt the rest of the batch instead of waiting it out. Confirmed via a dialog before it takes effect. Attendees not yet emailed are skipped; anyone already sent the email keeps it, since that can't be undone. The panel's stat tiles, progress bar, and done-state summary now also account for cancelled recipients.
- Event Settings → Wallet's Samsung Wallet switch is now a real, saveable setting instead of a permanently disabled placeholder. Reports' Wallet platform breakdown, the Attendees table's Wallet column, and the attendee-detail Wallet card all now show or hide a Samsung entry to match - same as the existing Apple/Google toggles. PassCreator has no Samsung Wallet API yet, so no attendee gets an actual Samsung pass and the new Samsung rows always read "Not supported yet" / show a muted icon; this only prepares the toggle and every surface that reflects it for when that support lands.
- Saving Event Settings' name, date, timezone, event hours, event type, or Apple Wallet toggle - or the Location tab's venue name, address, directions/accessibility notes, or entrance/gate/opening-hours details - now shows a confirmation with the number of attendees whose already-installed wallet pass will be pushed an update, when there's at least one - previously this cascade fired silently. Editing an attendee's name, email, company, department, or ticket type shows a similar, non-blocking note when that attendee already has an installed wallet pass.
- Attendees' header "More actions" has a new "Push updates" item (once the event has Wallet configured) that pushes the latest name/ticket type/event details to every already-installed wallet pass across the whole event at once, for when a pass needs refreshing but nothing wallet-relevant actually changed. Shows up in Event Settings → Wallet's push history as "Whole event · manual push".
- Attendees' selection bulk bar has two new "More actions" items, "Set company" and "Set department" - type one value and apply it to every selected attendee at once, next to the existing "Change ticket type"/"Change attendance status" bulk edits.
- Attendees' selection bulk bar has a new "Refresh status" wallet action, next to the existing "Push updates" - pulls the current device-registration status straight from the provider for every selected attendee's wallet pass at once, instead of one at a time from each attendee's own page.
- Attendees' header "More actions" has a new "Refresh status" item (once the event has Wallet configured) that pulls the current device-registration status from the provider for every wallet pass across the whole event at once, including a voided one - runs in the background and reports a summary toast once it finishes.
- `/.well-known/change-password` now redirects to the right password-change page for whoever's asking, following the W3C "Well-Known URL for Changing Passwords" convention Safari, Chrome, and several password managers already look for - a normal signed-in staff member lands on My Account's own "Change password" section, while someone mid-way through a required password reset lands on that dedicated flow instead - so a browser or password manager's own "change password" shortcut always works, instead of guessing (or, for most staff, bouncing them straight back to sign-in).
- Settings → Security has a new "Autofill passkey suggestions" toggle, nested under "Passkey sign-in on the login page" (and disabled until that one is on). Turning it on runs the same passkey sign-in ceremony via WebAuthn conditional mediation, so a saved passkey shows up as a browser autofill suggestion directly in the sign-in page's email field instead of requiring a click on "Sign in with a passkey" first. Off by default; the explicit "Sign in with a passkey" button keeps working exactly the same either way.

### Changed

- Attendees' header "More" button now reads "More actions" at desktop widths, matching the label the selection bulk bar's own menu already uses (still shortened to "More" below 768px).

- Attendees, Attendee Detail, and Reports now respect an event's Wallet platform toggles (Event Settings → Wallet). Turning off the whole feature hides the Attendees table's Wallet column, the attendee-detail Wallet card and status chip, and the Reports Wallets tab (its export options are unavailable too); turning off just Apple or just Google Wallet drops that platform's icon, card row, and report chart slice everywhere those surfaces appear, without affecting the other platform.
- Mail settings validation errors (Organisation and per-event Mail tabs, and the setup wizard) now show inline on the specific field that's wrong, with a red border and message, instead of a single list at the bottom of the page. Save shows a "Please fix the highlighted fields" notification and scrolls to the first problem field.
- From address, Reply-to, Envelope from, Mailbox, and Allowed from domain now check that the domain's top-level part is a real, currently delegated one (for example rejecting a typo like "example.con" or a placeholder like "mail.local"), not just that it looks roughly email-shaped.
- Communication → Send's bulk-send progress now shows Sent/Failed/Remaining stat tiles and a two-segment progress bar while a batch drains, and a "Send complete" summary card once it finishes, instead of a single plain-text line. The "Send another" button is now hidden until the batch has actually finished draining - it previously appeared as soon as sending started, and clicking it mid-send stopped the page from tracking that batch (with no way to check on it again) without cancelling anything server-side, so an operator could unknowingly fire a second, concurrent send while the first was still in flight.
- Requirements no longer shows an item's or custom field's internal slug (e.g. `giftbag`, `t_shirt_size`) under its display name in the Event items list, the Custom attendee fields list, or the "Attendee data field" picker - these are purely internal identifiers with no bearing on how operators or admins use the feature, so they're no longer part of the everyday view. The slug still reappears in parentheses, but only for a name that collides with another item's or field's (both only require the slug to be unique, not the display name) - otherwise two same-named rows, or checkboxes in the picker, would be impossible to tell apart.
- Communication → Delivery log, Attendees, and Attendee Detail now recognize a "Cancelled" mail-delivery status (styled distinctly from a delivery failure), and the Attendees page's mail-status "Not sent" filter now also includes attendees whose only delivery was cancelled - they still need a ticket exactly like someone who was never queued.
- Event Settings page split into per-tab components (`EventGeneralInfoPanel`, `EventImagesPanel`, `EventWalletPanel`, `EventDangerZonePanel`) and extracted handler functions, cutting the page's cognitive complexity; the shared form-panel prop type and logo-aware settings footer are also deduplicated across the panels (no behavior change).
- Check-in behaviour (issue badge at entry, require confirmation on scan, allow manual lookup, auto-advance after a valid check-in) moved out of Requirements into its own "Check-in behaviour" tab in Event Settings, alongside Requirements' other settings-adjacent tabs - Requirements now only covers event items and custom attendee fields. The four toggles now save together via Save/Reset, matching every other Event Settings tab, instead of saving individually the instant each was flipped.

### Fixed

- Attendees' Wallet column rendered the Samsung Wallet icon visibly smaller than its Apple/Google neighbors despite sharing the same font-size, because the SVG kept a large margin of transparent space around the mark inside its own box. The icon is now cropped to the mark's real bounds, matching the visual size of the two Tabler glyphs beside it.
- Attendees' mobile/tablet card view showed each field's name ("Pass"/"Attendance"/"Mail") as plain text right next to its colored status badge, which could read as a continuation of the badge instead of a separate label, and - once "Attendance" needed enough room - regularly pushed "Mail" onto its own line. Each field name is now a small icon with the same name available on hover/focus (the same pattern the Wallet column's own platform icons already use), which both keeps the three fields on one line and makes each one visually distinct from its badge.
- CSS custom-property fallback values for spacing, radius, shadow, and typography tokens (not just color, which was already fixed) now match their real defined values across the admin panel, the public ticket page, and the shared `@admitto/ui` package - the automated coverage check that already caught color-token drift now also covers these three token files.
- Settings → Identity's disabled "SAML" protocol tile and Settings → Branding's "faux bold/italic" font-preview hints now use the app's real tooltip (announced to screen readers, reachable by keyboard) instead of a native browser title attribute that only showed on mouse hover. Attendees' bulk-selection "Clear selection" button now has a visible focus ring, matching every other icon-only button in the app.
- Settings → Archiving no longer silently drops the connection-state banner when the events list fails to load - a 401 or 5xx now flags the same shared connection-state indicator every other events-list screen already reports through.
- Organisation and per-event Mail settings no longer jump when Save is clicked with an invalid field - clicking Save repeatedly used to re-scroll the page every time, even when the error was already visible.
- SMTP advanced tuning fields (rate limit, max connections, max messages, connection/greeting/socket timeouts) that fail validation are no longer silently dropped on save with no feedback - they're now checked and show an error like every other field.
- Text fields, selects, and searchable-select/phone-country search boxes on mobile/touch devices now render at the same visual size as their desktop 14px counterparts, instead of visibly larger. The underlying computed font-size is unchanged (still 16px, which is what stops iOS Safari from auto-zooming the page on focus) - the field is instead rendered at that size and then scaled back down to the desktop box's exact dimensions, so the protection against iOS's zoom-on-focus still applies. Multi-line text areas are unaffected (still a plain 16px on touch devices, as before).
- Requirements → Event items' Active toggle is now vertically centered in its row, matching the item name and description next to it - it previously sat a couple pixels above center.
- Editing an event's custom field definition (for example toggling "Required") no longer re-sends its select options as a side effect. Previously any save re-derived and rewrote the full options list from the edit form regardless of whether the operator touched it, which could silently diverge from the list an attendee's already-saved value was chosen against - once that happened, the attendee's saved selection stopped matching any current option, so it showed as unset in Edit attendee and had to be re-picked before the form could be saved again.
- Communication → Delivery log no longer silently drops rows when "Rows per page" is set to 200. The API capped the actual page size at 100 regardless of what was requested, while the "Showing X-Y of Z" / page count still reflected the full total - so a 200-per-page view looked like it was missing entries and its page count didn't match what was on screen. The cap now matches the 200 option the dropdown already offered.
- An event item's "Attendee data field" picker (Requirements page) no longer lets the same custom field be selected on more than one item. Nothing previously stopped it, so the same hint (for example "Shirt size: L") could silently render on two different items' check-in cards for no reason. The picker now grays out a field already claimed by another item, with a tooltip naming which one, and saving a config that references a field another item already has is rejected server-side as a defense-in-depth backstop against concurrent edits - the conflict check now always re-reads on a fresh connection right after acquiring the per-event lock, closing a gap where a create running concurrently with a disabling/badge-affecting edit (which needs a stricter transaction level for an unrelated reason) could still use a stale, pre-lock-wait view of the other items and let both succeed.
- My account's "Add" button for a passkey or security key with none registered yet no longer disappears entirely when the instance-wide passkey/security-key feature is turned off - it now stays visible but disabled, and the explanation underneath renders as a proper notice box instead of plain text, matching every other persistent notice on the page.
- Small wording and color-token consistency fixes across the admin panel: the "Event archived"/"Event unarchived" confirmation now reads the same wherever it appears, Reports' and Attendees' load-error messages now say "Could not load..." like every other screen instead of "Failed to load...", Settings → Identity's error titles now say "Could not load" instead of "Couldn't load", and a leftover reference to two color variables that were never actually defined (on the event-archiving error text) now points at the same token the rest of the app uses for error text.
- Settings → External services (weather and maps provider save/test) and an event's Wallet connection test now show which specific field is wrong when validation fails (for example "API key is required for this Open-Meteo host."), instead of a blanket "Check the form and try again." The server was already computing this detail and sending it; the admin client just wasn't reading it.
- About 90 error conditions across the admin panel (a missing attendee/item/session ID, a wallet action that's already running, a ticket type conflict, an unset Cloudflare Access policy, and more) now show a specific message instead of falling back to whatever generic text the screen happened to use. A new automated check now fails the build if a new error code ships without one of these messages (or its own dedicated handling), so this can't silently drift out of coverage again.
- Communication → Templates now shows which action actually failed (for example "Save failed.", "Create failed.", "Preview failed.") when a save, create, load, or preview request errors out, instead of a single generic "Request failed." for every case - the success toast for the same actions was already this specific, only the failure side was generic.
- The public ticket page's "Access denied" and "Something went wrong" error pages now use the same red as every other error state in the app, instead of no color at all. The wallet-add error message and the revoked/cancelled ticket notice now also use the app's design tokens instead of a hardcoded red that didn't quite match, and the revoked/cancelled notice is now announced to screen readers as an alert instead of a routine status update.
- Settings → Identity now shows the actual reason when identity providers or the Cloudflare Access configuration fail to load (for example the specific OIDC discovery error), instead of a fixed "something went wrong" message that never reflected what actually failed.
- The "Revoke check-in?" confirmation now shows the same amber warning styling everywhere it appears (Attendee detail, and the check-in card), matching the bulk "Revoke check-in" action on the Attendees page. The single-attendee version previously showed the stronger red "danger" styling for the same easily-reversible action ("They can check in again at any time"), while every other reversible revoke action in the app (bulk check-in, bulk items) already used the amber warning treatment - red is now reserved for the less-reversible actions, like revoking a wallet pass.
- Adding an attendee or editing one's attribute fields now shows which specific field is wrong and why (for example "Dietary is required." or "Shirt size must be one of: S, M, L.") when the server rejects the save, instead of one generic "check required attribute fields and option values" message that gave no hint what to actually fix.
- Around 30 load-error messages across the admin panel (settings panels, attendee/communication/reports screens, session and role management, the setup wizard) now consistently say "Could not load X", matching the rest of the app's wording, instead of a mix of "Could not load" and "Failed to load" for the same kind of error.
- Settings → Identity's Cloudflare Access and identity provider editors now show the app's own "Discard unsaved changes?" confirmation dialog when leaving with unsaved edits, instead of the browser's native confirm popup - matching the confirmation style used everywhere else in the admin panel.
- The "Your authenticator or backup code" field shown when a superadmin resets another user's password/two-factor/sessions now matches the same label style used everywhere else in the app, instead of a slightly different shade of gray left over from before that field grew passkey support.
- Communication → Templates' "Send test" result showed a raw, lowercase "send failed" for an unrecognized send error, instead of the same "Send failed." wording every other mail test-send screen (Settings → Mail transport, bounce detection) already used for the same kind of failure.
- A Microsoft Graph send that fails because the token response came back without an access token (a malformed provider response, not a normal auth rejection) is now retried like every other unclassified mail-transport failure, instead of being treated as permanent after a single attempt.
- The "Discard unsaved changes?" confirmation (Communication template editor, Event settings) no longer shows the stronger red "danger" styling - it now matches the same, already-correct treatment used for the identical action on the Attendee detail and Setup wizard pages. Nothing is actually lost permanently (the form can always be filled in again), so this matches how the app treats every other fully-reversible confirmation.
- Several load-error boxes across the admin panel (Requirements, Audit log, Security audit log, Events picker, My account, session bootstrap, Communication deliveries, wallet push history, Cloudflare Access, and an identity provider editor) showed one wording in the title and a different one in the message underneath - for example a box titled "Could not load audit log" whose text said "Failed to load audit log." All now say the same thing. Attendees' export and Check-in's transport/lookup error handling had the same "Request failed." vs a differently-worded fallback mismatch already fixed elsewhere in the app.
- 42 CSS color-token fallback values across the admin panel (and one on the public ticket page's type badge, the only one actually visible - a shade of gray so close to its neighbor it's imperceptible in practice) had drifted from the real value defined in the app's own design tokens - some looked like hand-typed approximations rather than the copied value. All now match exactly, and a new automated check fails the build if a fallback drifts again.
- "Remember this device" no longer stops working whenever your network's IP address changes. It previously required an exact match to the IP address recorded when you checked the box, so anything that changes it - switching Wi-Fi, using a VPN, or an ISP/mobile carrier that reassigns a new address on reconnect (routine for many home internet providers) - silently fell back to asking for your two-factor code again, well before the actual trust period (30 days by default) ran out. Trust now follows the device's cookie alone, matching how "remember this device" works on most other sites; the IP and browser recorded when you checked the box are no longer read back to decide whether the cookie is accepted.
- The event timezone picker on "Create event" now actually marks itself required for screen readers. The `required` prop was already being passed in and was accepted by the component, but nothing inside it used it, so the control's `aria-required` attribute was never set.

### Security

- Superadmins can now see in Logs & Audit when a "remember this device" cookie skipped the two-factor step at login, not just when a device was first remembered. Every prior MFA outcome already left an audit trail except this one - added as the compensating control for the "remember this device" fix above, so a stolen password combined with a stolen trusted-device cookie still leaves a queryable trace even though it's no longer blocked by an IP mismatch.
- Reports → Wallets' charts now run on `recharts` (MIT) instead of `apexcharts`/`react-apexcharts`, which switched to a revenue-gated dual license (as of the pinned versions) that forbids free-tier redistribution in a self-hosted, redistributed toolkit like Admitto. No visible or behavioral change to the charts themselves.
- CI's `pii-guard` job, which already blocks a pull request over a real (non-`example.com`/`test.com`) email address in tracked `.csv`/`.tsv`/`.json` data files, now also blocks over a phone-number-shaped string in that same file scope plus `.yaml`/`.yml`/`.sql`. The pattern is deliberately conservative (a leading `+` with digit-boundary guards) to avoid flagging version strings, hashes, or other digit sequences unrelated to phone numbers.
- The Event day, Wallets, and Custom fields Reports JSON endpoints now send `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a shared or public computer can no longer replay an event's admission stats, wallet adoption figures, or custom-field answers from browser cache after the admin signs out.
- The `app` container's per-request access log (`LOG_HTTP_REQUESTS=1`) now includes the client IP address for every request, not just authenticated staff/operator sessions - the app already reads it on every ticket/QR/check-in request to key its rate limiter, so this surfaces existing data for the traffic most worth watching for token scanning or brute-forcing, matching standard access-log practice and OWASP's logging guidance. Ticket/QR paths still never show the raw token (`/t/[redacted]`, `/q/[redacted]`); each now also carries a short one-way `ref` hash so repeated hits on the same participant's link are recognizable across log lines without exposing it.

---

### Deploy
- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto:0.6.4` (rolling `:0.6`)
- Migrations apply **automatically on container start**. **No manual `migrate deploy`.** Back up the database yourself before upgrading (the stack no longer takes an automatic pre-migration backup).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/solarssk/admitto/blob/v0.6.4/CHANGELOG.md)
